title: Feat: HTMLResponse should support `__html__` conversion of content
body:
### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc). ### Commit to Help - [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python from fastapi import FastAPI from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse class CustomHTML: def __html__(self) -> str: return "

Hello

" app = FastAPI() @app.get("/") def root(): return HTMLResponse(CustomHTML()) ``` ### Description Gets AttributeError because HTMLResponse only takes str and won't try to `__html__` to convert it into `str` first. Expected: return the str given by `content.__html__()`. Implementation: ```python if hasattr(content, "__html__"): content = content.__html__() ``` ### Operating System Other ### Operating System Details _No response_ ### FastAPI Version 0.139.0 ### Pydantic Version 2.13.4 ### Python Version 3.14 ### Additional Context The `__html__` method is a widely used method for signaling safe HTML output (that needs no escaping, and that isn't repr for which there is `_repr_html_`). This is used by templating and web frameworks (Django, Jinja2, Sanic).
